p.i: gil.lib.7. Pars mihi pacis erit, dextram tetigisse Tyran-ni. Valer. Maxim. lib.5. c.5. Bonfin.libr.7. decad.1.
Hodie quoque dexterarum coniunctione salutare solemus. Pithæus lib.1. Aduersar. cap.7. vbi Iob c.30.13. Eccl.c.29. explicatur, & Pierus in suis Hieroglyphicis lib.3f.

main_text.p: Ad genua vel pedes procidere, siue procumbere, ea attingere, exosculari denique in salutationibus & supplicationib.veteres consueuerūt, vti ex Homero, Virgil.lib.3.& 10. Ouid.lib.9. Metamorph.& 13. Plauto in Rudente, Liuio lib.45. Suetonius in Tybe.& Claudio,2. Reg.c.4. Genes.c.48.12. Stuck. d.loco. probat.

Pedum exosculatio vsitata quoque fuit in salutationibus & supplicationibus veterum. Luc. c.7.& osculum mutuum. Exod. c.18. Genes.c.33. c.39. Tob.c.7. Genes.c.45. Luc.c.15.1. Reg cap.19.20. Genes.c.48.10. Ruth.c.1. Genes.c.31. 2 Sam. cap.19. Tob.c.10. ex quibus constat, ludæis vsitatas fuisse salutationes per osculum in congressu & digressu amicorum.

Erat etiam quandoque osculum reconciliationis symbolum, vti 2.Sam.c.14. Luc.c.15. vel virtutis approbatæ in alio, 3. Efd.c.4. Prou.c.24. Matt.c.26.2.Sam.c.20.c.15. vide Cæl. Rhodigin.libr. 15.c.9.& lib.4.c.3. Plutar.in Probl.problem.6. Pier. in Hieroglyph.
Ab osculo differt basium, quod est pudicorum affectuum; & suauium, quod libidinum, vel amoris; cum osculum officiorum sit habitus & gestus.
Pompon. Latus in compend. Rom. hist. dicit Imperatores suas manus osculandas suis nobilibus

page.notes: Old-style long s printed as s throughout; several Latin citations are set in italic and partly illegible in the scan (e.g. "Aduersar.", "Tyran-ni"), transcribed as printed where readable. Some words in the lower third are faint.
